How htmlnet works

A neural network computed in HTML and CSS. Checkboxes are input bits. CSS custom properties carry the signals. The browser's style engine does the math. The one <script> only turns drags into checkbox clicks; delete it and the network still runs.

Bits

A checkbox is the only state on the page. A selector turns it into a registered integer:

@property --x { syntax: "<integer>"; inherits: true; initial-value: 0; }
body.rt:has(#x:checked) { --x: 1; }

Every other signal is a declaration that reads earlier signals with var(). Click a checkbox and the browser recomputes everything downstream.

Gates

Four native CSS operations, read as logic on 0 and 1:

gateCSS
NOT acalc(1 - a)
a AND bmin(a, b)
a OR bmax(a, b)
a XOR bcalc(max(a, b) - min(a, b))

Everything else is those four, wired together at build time: half adder (XOR + AND), full adder, ripple-carry adder, AND-gate multiplier, two's-complement negation. A neuron is a weighted sum plus a bias; its output is NOT the sign bit, so 1 when the sum is ≥ 0.

CSS can multiply directly with calc(var(--a) * var(--b)). Gate mode is a teaching choice, not a workaround. The demo's comparison section runs the same XOR and matrix rows with eight native declarations.

XOR

One linear neuron can't learn XOR. Two hidden neurons can:

h1  = step(+2x1 - 2x0 - 1)
h2  = step(-2x1 + 2x0 - 1)
out = step(+2h1 + 2h2 - 1)

A hidden layer is just more named signals that a later neuron reads. That's all "layers stack" means here. This network is a separate example; it doesn't feed the digit classifier.

The digit classifier

The canvas is 196 invisible checkboxes (14×14). Two gate stages shrink your drawing to what the classifier was trained on:

  1. Dilation. Each cell ORs with its four neighbors, so a thin stroke survives the next step.
  2. Downsample. Each 2×2 block ORs into one bit. That gives a 7×7 grid, shown as "network sees".

The classifier is linear: 49 bits × 10 rows of weights in [−3, 3]. Each weight splits into two bit planes, so scores come from gate popcounts instead of a multiplier. A gate tournament picks the highest score, and OR-trees light the seven-segment display straight from gate signals.

The decimal numbers on the page are display-only calc() views. They never feed back into the circuit.

Build

Two Rust programs run at build time and never ship. train/ trains the weights on MNIST, running the same dilation and downsample the page uses. gen/ compiles the circuit and writes about 6,834 CSS signals into one 1.6 MB file. It opens from file://: no server, no network, no WASM.

Source: github.com/diegoperez956/html-neural-net. MIT licensed.
